A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BAC research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original robotic simulation evaluations, component ablations, caching-error experiments, and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds physical-robot experiments, RDT-1B evaluations, and further diagnostic and sampler-compatibility experiments.

M1.justification: The cosine-similarity-based ACS optimization, dynamic programming solver, upstream-block selection, and BUA schedule union remain unchanged. Renaming k to n and applying BAC to additional models and samplers do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 adds physical manipulation of a deformable bag using a Franka Research 3 arm and four ManiSkill tasks evaluated with RDT-1B. These substantially extend the earlier simulation coverage, while retaining Robomimic, Push-T, Block Pushing, and Kitchen.

E2.justification: v1 primarily compares BAC with full-computation DP-T and Uniform caching. v2 adds evaluated TeaCache comparisons in Table 1 and DDIM comparisons in the physical experiment and Appendix A.16, substantially broadening the acceleration methods considered.

E3.justification: Table 1 replaces Uniform's explicit S=7/10 configurations with fast/fastest configurations having different reported FLOPs. New protocols include physical inference-frequency and latency measurements, DDIM with K=40 and BAC S=3/5/10 at n=3, and homogeneity analysis using 50 episodes per task across eight layers and ten timesteps.

E4.justification: v2 adds physical failure-case analysis, FFN-versus-attention weight-norm analysis, detailed cached-versus-ground-truth feature comparisons, expanded episode-homogeneity analysis, and DDIM compatibility tests. The earlier component, hyperparameter, similarity-metric, and error-propagation studies are largely retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.15 and Table 29 newly report inter-episode similarity standard deviations and fifth/ninety-fifth percentiles. This adds statistical characterization of feature variability; the original benchmark practice of averaging across three training seeds remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Original BAC entries in Table 1 remain unchanged, but v2 adds TeaCache results, replaces Uniform configuration results, and reports physical-robot, RDT-1B, homogeneity, and DDIM-plus-BAC outcomes. For example, the new physical experiment reports BAC achieving 71% success at 39.2 Hz. These are added or differently configured results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The ACS mathematical formulation, FFN perturbation propositions, regularity assumptions, and first-order derivation are retained. The proof moves from Appendix A.1 to A.4 without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of training-free block-wise caching, optimal ACS scheduling, BUA-based error-propagation mitigation, and approximately threefold acceleration without performance degradation. The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion preserve their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking FFN amplification to larger weight norms, physical failures to observation-action desynchronization, and DDIM results to complementary acceleration. It also interprets the new cache-behavior and homogeneity evidence. The limitations discussion retains weak-base-model accuracy but removes v1's explicit caveat about lacking real-world VLA experiments.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the physical robot, camera, and real-world n=3 setting, adds a project-page address, and states an intention to release implementation instructions. Existing checkpoint links remain. However, fast/fastest comparator labels replace explicit Uniform update budgets without equivalent configuration details.

R1.justification: v2 adds RDT-1B as a cited model and discusses compatibility with sampling-based acceleration. Most prior-work positioning is retained or relocated. TeaCache's underlying paper was already cited in v1, so its evaluation is not a newly introduced literature connection.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains recognizable. v2 condenses and relocates VLA background, moves and shortens limitations, reorganizes experiments into physical and simulation subsections, and adds ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements. It also changes k to n and updates authorship and conference formatting.

P2.justification: v2 splits the original framework figure, expands the main comparison table, replaces the detailed component-ablation table with a bar chart, and adds physical-robot, VLA, weight-norm, cache-feature, and homogeneity displays. These substantially change the visual presentation beyond renumbering and pagination.

improvement.justification: Physical-robot validation, simulated VLA evaluation, additional acceleration baselines, and DDIM compatibility tests substantially address gaps in v1's practical and generalization evidence. Reporting weaknesses remain: new protocols are incompletely specified, the RDT-1B paragraph disagrees with Figure 7a about the lossless setting, and Table 29's Push-T mean of 0.9285 contradicts the claimed minimum of 0.96. These issues limit particular conclusions but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical validation.
